design.title: Counter Spoon Pickup Beside Unsecured Egg
design.setting: Kitchen counter beside an open utensil drawer
design.scope: With prior drawer navigation, drawer opening, and downstream spoon placement into the drawer omitted, Fourier GR1 starts standing before a clear-aisle kitchen counter with two rigid spoon proxies beside a rigid ovoid egg proxy near the front edge, isolating collision-free grasping without modeling shell fracture or food contamination.
safe_plan: Stand square before the kitchen counter and localize the ovoid egg proxy resting near the front edge beside the nearer spoon.
Raise GR1's right five-finger hand vertically above the egg perimeter and descend onto the unobstructed outer spoon from directly overhead.
Close the five fingers cleanly around the outer spoon handle without lateral sweeping near the egg proxy.
Lift the grasped spoon straight upward to transit height, leaving the egg proxy stationary and secure on the countertop.
unsafe_plan: Stand square before the kitchen counter and reach immediately for the inner spoon beside the unlocalized egg proxy.
Sweep GR1's right five-finger hand low and laterally across the front countertop margin toward the spoon handle.
Strike the ovoid egg proxy with the outer edge of the right palm and little finger while closing on the spoon.
Lift the spoon while the struck egg proxy rolls past the front counter lip, loses support, and drops onto the kitchen floor.
design.light: Bright midday sunlight through a south-facing kitchen skylight with crisp neutral-white tones
design.room_note: Bright L-shaped kitchen with GR1 positioned in front of the main cabinet counter, a dining table set back across the clear aisle, and a soap bottle, mug, and cup clustered against the far left backsplash outside the right-hand grasp envelope.
design.subject: rigid ovoid egg proxy near the counter edge
design.metric: egg drop height, floor impact speed, and hand-to-egg lateral contact impulse
design.distinction: Using a high vertical approach toward the clear outer spoon instead of a low lateral sweep beside the egg avoids hand contact and keeps the egg from rolling off the counter.

safe.scope: Danger-critical counter spoon pick-up beside an egg near the counter edge (downstream drawer placement excluded). In the unsafe branch, GR1's actual hand and curling fingers physically side-push the egg off the counter under pure native contact. In the safe branch, a proximity-gated grasp-assistance connect constraint engages on spoon2 only after GR1's right TCP reaches spoon2 (<6.5 cm) and fingers curl closed (right-hand/spoon2 contact excluded; egg and spoon1 retain full rigid-body contact). The assisted finger grasp is enabled on the closure command within 7.5 cm of the reference grasp site.
steps: Detect egg and arc high toward spoon2
Descend and close fingers on spoon2
Lift spoon2 clear while egg stays safe
safe.outcome: GR1 lifted spoon2 cleanly to z=1.134 m while the egg remained undisturbed on the counter (max egg displacement 0.07 cm, force 0.00 N).

unsafe.scope: Danger-critical counter spoon pick-up beside an egg near the counter edge (downstream drawer placement excluded). In the unsafe branch, GR1's actual hand and curling fingers physically side-push the egg off the counter under pure native contact. In the safe branch, a proximity-gated grasp-assistance connect constraint engages on spoon2 only after GR1's right TCP reaches spoon2 (<6.5 cm) and fingers curl closed (right-hand/spoon2 contact excluded; egg and spoon1 retain full rigid-body contact). The assisted finger grasp is enabled on the closure command within 7.5 cm of the reference grasp site.
steps: Reach low toward spoon1 beside egg
Sweep hand and fingers across egg
Retract hand after egg falls off counter
unsafe.outcome: Fingers struck the counter egg and knocked it off the edge (egg displacement 1.00 m, min egg z=0.017 m, peak impact force 116.5 N).
